Author: Farjand Ali Bench: Farjand Ali

HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous (Petition) No. 2503/2021 Ravindra Singh Son Of Daljeet Singh, R/o 1017, Chanakya Puri Near Sheela Cinema Rohatak Haryana.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through P.p.
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Abdul Kalam Khan through VC For Respondent(s) : Mr. M.S. Saini, PP HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 19/01/2022

The instant miscellaneous petition has been preferred on behalf of the petitioner challenging the order dated 07.01.2021 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, No. 2, Kota in Criminal Regular Case No. 4391/2016 titled as State v. Pankaj & Ors. for the offence under Sections 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act whereby the application filed by the petitioner for conversion of process has been rejected.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, No. 2, Kota
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The criminal revision preferred against the said order has also been dismissed vide order dated 01.02.2021 by the learned Additional District Judge, No. 5, Kota in Revision Petition No. 27/2021.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Gone through the contents of FIR and the material made available on record.

It is reflecting from the order passed by the Court below that upon a complaint filed under the penal provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, learned Magistrate took cognizance of the offence and issued process for the presence of the accused- petitoner.

The service of notice, summon or bailable warrant was (2 of 2) [CRLMP-2503/2021] never affected upon the accused, however,
looking to the long pendency of the case, the learned Magistrate deemed it appropriate to call the petitioner through warrant of arrest.

As soon the accused-petitioner got to know about issuance of warrant of arrest, he through his counsel moved an application under Section 70(2) of Cr.P.C. for conversion of process which has been rejected vide order dated 07.01.2021 and thereafter, the revision petition has also been rejected.
Both the orders have been challenged here in this petition.
The petitioner is a 61 years old man.
No service of any regular process was ever affected upon him.

The matter is under the penal provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, therefore, looking to the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow the petition.

sentences.text: The standing warrant of arrest too is quashed and set aside.
The petitioner shall appear before the learned Trial Court on or before 28.02.2022.
In the event, he appears and moves an application, he shall be released on bail on the very same day provided he furnishes bail bonds to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court.
